bug_semantics: The Flint/direct-query dispatcher classifies CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW as a Flint extension statement and forwards the whole string to Apache Spark without validating the inner SQL. The Flint grammar captures that inner query as an opaque token sequence (materializedViewQuery : .+?), so prohibited Spark SQL (TRANSFORM ... USING 'cmd', reflect/java System calls, CREATE FUNCTION, and other grammar-deny-list elements) that is blocked on the ordinary SQL path still executes on Spark workers. A remote authenticated user with async/direct-query access can therefore RCE by wrapping the payload in CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW ... AS <denied SQL>.
flaw_origin: PR #2336 first added Flint CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW support: grammar rule materializedViewQuery as a catch-all, isIndexQuery() treating CREATE MV as a Flint/index query, and SparkQueryDispatcher submitting that raw query to EMR/Spark with no inner-SQL check. Later SQL grammar deny-list (#3039) and UDF restriction (#2790) were wired only onto the non-Flint branch, so the MV wrapper became a bypass. #3096 added validateFlintExtensionQuery() as an explicit no-op; #5485 is the first implementation that extracts IndexQueryDetails.mvQuery and runs it through the deny list.
